extracted.intended_audience: New York State agency staff and counsel preparing and filing rulemakings (State Register/NYCRR) under SAPA
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for state agency staff on preparing, filing, publishing and complying with New York rulemaking notices, supporting statements (RIS/RFA/RAFA/JIS), emergency and adoption procedures, and Executive Chamber/RRU review for inclusion in the State Register and NYCRR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage of Must/Should/May
rubrics_metrics.description: Must is used to denote a required action. Should denotes an action recommended by the Department of State’s Division of Administrative Rules, but which is not required. May is used for purely discretionary actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual establishes this precise word scheme and expects authors/preparers to use these words consistently to reflect requirement level in notices and attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use prescribed notice forms
rubrics_metrics.description: You must use the Notice of Proposed Rule Making form to initiate a rule making; Department-prescribed forms and formats must be used for all rule making notices and attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms and formats are available at http://www.dos.ny.gov/info/e-file/e-forms.html. There is a specific Notice of Proposed Rule Making (Rate Making) form for SAPA §102(2)(a)(ii) rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority citation must be specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a legal citation of the statutory authority that authorizes or empowers your agency to propose the rule; it must be as specific as possible (cite subdivision/paragraph).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citation formats: Name of law followed by sections and subdivisions; separate multiple laws with semicolons. Include chaptered law citations or US Code citations where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject and purpose field constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject of the rule: make it short (limited characters). Purpose of the rule: begin every purpose with the word 'To' and explain, briefly, why the rule is needed or what it will accomplish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subject and purpose populate the State Register and indexes; keep them concise and avoid summarizing the entire text in the Purpose—if needed, elaborate in attached statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public hearings: scheduling and effect on timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: You must indicate whether a hearing is scheduled; if a hearing is mandated by statute, you cannot hold it until at least 45 days after publication and must continue to accept comments for 5 days after the last scheduled hearing; proposals with scheduled hearings expire 365 days after the last scheduled hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish mandated vs optional hearings on the form. Mandated hearings affect the rulemaking schedule and minimum comment periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreter services and accessibility for hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: If a public hearing is scheduled, the agency must provide interpreter services to hearing-impaired persons upon written request and must ensure hearings are reasonably accessible to persons with mobility impairments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a location is not suitable for mobility impairment, identify the location and indicate efforts made to provide an accessible hearing site; include statement on availability of interpreter services in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text attachments: full text vs summary, word limits and posting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the full text is more than 2,000 words, you must create and attach a summary under 2,000 words; if a summary is used, the full text must be posted on a State website or the proposal is subject to a 60-day comment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nearly all text attachments must be in MS Word (NOT pdf). For 102(2)(a)(ii) rules you may attach a description in lieu of full text or summary. Use the paperclip attachment feature on the pdf form to attach documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text formatting (visual and typing conventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Text must indicate deletions by bracketing and additions by underlining (no strikethroughs); must include brief written instructions indicating action type and location; type double-spaced, unjustified, with a five-character indent for each paragraph; use plain manuscript style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit only the text being amended (not whole parts). Specific page/print conventions: plain white 8.5x11 paper, laser printer, narrow margins, first tab stop 5 characters from left, serif or sans-serif fonts in 10–12 pt. The Division may reject unreadable or overly formatted submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: All attachments must be MS Word (not PDF)
rubrics_metrics.description: All attachments to the Department of State rulemaking forms must be in MS Word format — NOT pdf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to text, RIS, RFA, RAFA, JIS and other attachments. The e-filing workflow requires MS Word attachments for proper processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text contact and submission contact information required
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 9 (Text contact) must identify the individual from whom the text and attached statements may be obtained (name, agency, office address, telephone, e-mail). Item 10 (Submission contact) must identify the person to whom public comments should be sent (if different).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if full text and statements are published, an agency contact must be specified for public requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum public comment periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum comment periods: 45 days after publication when full text is included or posted on a State website; 60 days after publication when a summary is included and text is not posted; 30 days for a revised proposal; 5 days after the last scheduled public hearing required by statute (unless statute specifies otherwise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may accept comments for longer than the minimum. The agency may set a longer deadline in Item 11, but cannot adopt the rule before that self-imposed deadline expires.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Register publication schedule and deadline week
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices filed between Wednesday and close of business the following Tuesday are published in the State Register issue dated 15 days after the deadline date; non-e-filed rulemakings have a noon Tuesday deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan submissions across a five-workday submission week (Wed–Tue). Last-minute problems can delay publication by at least a week. The Division has authority to reject material not meeting Executive Law, SAPA or DOS requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: RRU pre-submission review requirement for Executive-controlled agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies subject to the Governor’s executive control must submit all notices of proposed or revised rulemakings to RRU along with the full text and full text of each accompanying statement before submitting a proposal to DOS for publication (consensus-rule exception).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RRU will review and forward with recommendation to Executive Chamber offices; RRU may require additional analysis if review criteria are not met. For questions contact RRU directly; submit completed pdf and attachments by email to dob.sm.reg.submittal@budget.ny.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensus rule criteria and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: If no person is likely to object (e.g., repeal obsolete regulations, implement non-discretionary statutory provisions, technical, or otherwise non-controversial), an agency may propose a consensus rule. Consensus rules are exempt from RIS, RFA and RAFA requirements and are not subject to RRU review, but a JIS or explanation why JIS is unnecessary is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although Executive Chamber consent is not required prior to publication of a consensus notice, consultation with RRU is recommended. If any objection is received during the comment period, the agency must withdraw and proceed with the normal rulemaking process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal expiration rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, a proposal will expire 365 days after publication in the State Register or 365 days after the date of the last scheduled public hearing; proposals for 102(2)(a)(ii) rules (rates, wages, security authorizations, etc.) do not expire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you schedule hearings, expiration is 365 days after last scheduled hearing. Agencies frequently accept comments beyond the minimum periods; a proposal does not expire until the 365-day limit unless acted on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial revision definition and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Any addition, deletion or other change in the text of a proposed rule which materially alters its purpose, meaning or effect is a 'substantial revision'. Substantial revisions require submission of a Notice of Revised Rule Making (a second proposal) and will open an additional comment period; substantial revisions do not include mere definitions or clarifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For publication, the revised text must be compared to the originally proposed text (or the most recently published revision). A revised RIS/RFA/RAFA/JIS may be required if the change warrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency certification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Every State Register notice form ends with an agency certification to be completed by the person who prepared the form (not necessarily the agency head), certifying that the preparer reviewed the form and that it complies with SAPA and DOS requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Validate button on the pdf form to confirm the form 'verified ok' before saving and e-filing. Make any corrections indicated by validation failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Impact Statement (RIS) requirements and word rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Most proposals must be accompanied by an RIS. The RIS normally has a 2,000-word limit but may be expanded in 500-word increments for each abstract included (each study/data analysis abstract must not exceed 500 words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RIS Part A/Part B/Part C selection on the notice form: attach full text, summary, or consolidated RIS; or check exemption reason (consolidated RIS previously published; 102(2)(a)(ii) rule; consensus rule). If claiming SAPA §202-a exemption, attach a statement. Attachments must be MS Word.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (RFA) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: RFA requirements mirror RIS: select Part A if attaching full text/summary/consolidated RFA; Part B if claiming rule will not impose adverse economic impact (attach explanation); Part C for exemptions (consolidated RFA, 102(2)(a)(ii), consensus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you claim no adverse impact, attach a statement explaining the finding and reasons. All attachments must be MS Word.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural Area Flexibility Analysis (RAFA) content and process
rubrics_metrics.description: For 102(2)(a)(i) rules, RAFA must: (a) describe types and estimate number of rural areas affected; (b) describe reporting, recordkeeping and other compliance requirements and professional services needed; (c) estimate costs to implement and comply; (d) indicate how the rule was designed to minimize adverse impacts on rural areas; (e) describe how agency ensured participation of public and private interests in rural areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must consider approaches to minimize adverse impacts (differing compliance timetables, performance standards, exemptions that don't endanger welfare). '(a)(ii)' rules and rules with no adverse impacts on rural areas are exempt (agency must provide explanatory finding). Consolidated RAFAs allowed; revised RAFA required when info is inadequate or substantial revisions occur. Ensure public participation via notice, direct notification, special conferences, or procedural changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Job Impact Statement (JIS) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A JIS differs from RIS/RFA/RAFA: Part B allows an agency to state the rule will not have a substantial adverse effect on jobs (must attach explanation including summary of information and methodology unless effect is apparent); Part C allows consolidated JIS or exemptions (102(2)(a)(ii), submitted by Comptroller or Attorney General).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a JIS is not attached, specify the reason using the form parts and attach supporting statements where required. Attachments must be MS Word.

rubrics_metrics.name: RRU rule review criteria (authority & legislative purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule must be clearly within the authority delegated by law and must be consistent with and necessary to achieve a specific legislative purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RRU evaluates whether a rule exceeds authority or is needed to effect legislative objectives; if criteria unmet, further analysis may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: RRU rule review criteria (clarity and duplication)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule must be clearly written so that its meaning will be easily understood by those affected, and must not unnecessarily duplicate or exceed existing federal or state statutes or rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RRU checks for clear language and unnecessary overlaps with existing legal/regulatory materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: RRU rule review criteria (consistency, costs/benefits, mandates)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule must be consistent with existing state statutes and rules; produce public benefits outweighing costs; and not impose unfunded mandates on local governments or school districts except where statute requires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RRU looks for statutory consistency, cost-benefit justification, and whether local government mandates are funded when required by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: RRU rule review criteria (flexibility, innovation and least-burdensome approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule should prescribe methodologies or requirements allowing regulated parties flexibility and encourage innovation; give preference to the least costly, least burdensome regulatory and paperwork requirements needed to accomplish objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, favor performance standards and market-oriented solutions rather than prescriptive 'command-and-control' approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: RRU rule review criteria (risk assessment and evidence base)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule should be based on credible assessments, using recognized standards, of the degree and nature of the risks to be regulated, and based upon the best scientific, technical and economic information that can reasonably and affordably be obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RRU expects agencies to support rules with credible risk assessments and evidence; compare regulated risks with everyday familiar risks where useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for market-oriented and performance standards
rubrics_metrics.description: If possible and practical, rules should favor market-oriented solutions and performance standards over command-and-control regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of the RRU criteria to encourage flexibility, innovation and less prescriptive regulation when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and formats list requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department prescribes specific notice forms and formats (Notice of Proposed Rule Making, Notice of Revised Rule Making, Notice of Adoption, Notice of Emergency Adoption, Guidance Documents Certification, formats for RIS, RFA, RAFA, JIS, Regulatory Agenda, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the prescribed formats available on the DOS website; Appendix B lists required forms and formats and must be followed to ensure substantial compliance with SAPA regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency adoption timing and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice of Emergency Adoption may make a rule effective on a temporary basis for a maximum of 90 days from the date filed; re-adoptions tied to initiation of permanent proposal may be effective up to 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive Chamber approval is required for emergency adoptions. You cannot re-adopt an emergency unless a corresponding Notice of Proposed Rule Making is submitted to initiate permanent adoption process; see Chapter 4 for filing instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and distribution obligations (ARRC, RRU, Senate/Assembly)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the same time a rulemaking notice is submitted to DOS, a copy with full text and attached statements must also be sent to designated parties: Assembly ARRC, Senate ARRC and RRU. E-mail submission is recommended; Senate Majority Leader still requires a hard copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E-mail addresses: Assembly ARRC rulemaking@assembly.state.ny.us; Senate ARRC rulemaking@nysenate.gov; RRU dob.sm.reg.submittal@budget.ny.gov. Include full text for summaries and all required statements and attachments in the pdf form when submitting electronically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only submit text being amended
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit only the text being amended — do not send a whole Part or section when amending one section or subdivision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including extra text increases risk of unintentional adoption of accidental insertions or omissions. Keep submissions limited to necessary text and follow prescribed visual and written instructions for deletions/additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-year review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless contrary to another law, any rule adopted on or after January 1, 1997 shall be reviewed after five years and, thereafter, at five-year intervals; 5-year review does NOT apply to minor, obsolete, invalid rules and 102(2)(a)(ii) rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an agency decides a rule should continue without modification, it must publish a notice identifying the rule and statutory authority and include a reasoned justification and an assessment of public comments received in response to the regulatory agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submissions to Supreme Court Law Libraries for incorporation by reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials incorporated by reference into the NYCRR must be filed in specified formats with designated Supreme Court Law Libraries (electronic form preferred; microfiche/ultrafiche acceptable; otherwise rigid-bound or specified binder formats required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When electronic versions available include completed Incorporation by Reference Certification DOS-1196 with URL. Unsigned electronic certifications may be submitted to RRU and ARRC, but DOS will accept only signed hard copies. Appendix E details label, indexing and binding requirements and provides library addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling, indexing and binding requirements for hard-copy incorporation materials
rubrics_metrics.description: If materials cannot be provided electronically or on microfiche, bound volumes must be submitted with an adhesive label on front cover showing publication name, publisher, date, adopting agency, and cross-references to NYCRR sections; rigid-cover binders may not contain more than one publication/edition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loose-leaf publications must be in publisher loose-leaf binders; soft-bound publications fewer than 100 pages must be placed in a rigid-cover binder; special rules apply for self-covering publications. Request Chief Administrator exemption where impractical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and handling of prior emergency and amended adoptions
rubrics_metrics.description: You must specify the publication date and ID number of the most recent emergency previously published in the State Register for the same action being proposed; Chapter 3/4 explain how to adopt, amend, continue or withdraw emergency rules and file adoptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms exist for Notice of Emergency Adoption, Amended Notice of Adoption, Notice of Emergency Adoption and Proposed Rule Making, etc.; follow the prescribed forms and delivery instructions for adoptions and amended adoptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Agenda reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies specified by SAPA and the Governor must publish a Regulatory Agenda twice each year and complete Item 15 on the notice form indicating whether the action was included in the agenda and in which issue/year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 6 for Regulatory Agenda content and submission timing. Complete Item 15 when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of proposed rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may withdraw a Notice of Proposed Rule Making by submitting a Notice of Withdrawal form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the prescribed withdrawal form (see Appendix B) and file it with DOS for State Register publication.
